explanation: Mendel's monohybrid crosses established that each individual has two factors (alleles) for each trait, which separate during gamete formation and are restored to two during fertilization.

questions.q: What is the genetic constitution of the F1 generation in a monohybrid cross between two differing homozygous true-breeding parents?
questions.exp: Option C is correct because crossing two different homozygotes (AA x aa) yields offspring that are all heterozygous (Aa).
